source: The Social Network wins 3 Oscar Awards.
why: The files contain no Academy Award data, so the three Oscar wins cannot be reproduced.

source: X-rated Midnight Cowboy wins Best Picture
why: The files contain no Academy Award or MPAA rating data; the reproduced fact uses only the film's rank and its drugs, nudity and heroin theme tags.

source: The Rocky Horror Picture Show is the first popular to release to feature a number of LGBT themes.
why: The files have no release-width or popularity measure, so the claim that it was the first popular release with several LGBT themes cannot be tested; the #2 rank and the lgbt tag are reproduced.

source: Inspired by the success of The Passion of the Christ, faith-based films like God’s Not Dead rise and begin to break into the top 100 films.
why: God's Not Dead's 55th-place rank is reproduced, but the files' broad christianity tag does not show a clean rise in faith-based top-100 films after 2004 and includes many films that are not faith-based.

source: overall tagging begins to decline in 2013
why: The number of tagged films and keywords per film declines gradually from about 2010, not specifically from 2013; 2013 is higher than 2012.

source: Philadelphia dramatizes an AIDS discrimination case from 1986
why: The files record the film's 1993 production year and its aids/lgbt/anti-lgbt tags, but not the 1986 case year; the AIDS tag and rank are reproduced.

source: The role of “Philadelphia” in public discourse is unmatched.
why: This is an interpretive claim about public discourse, not a quantity measured in the files.
